written: 2026-09-28, prompted by Claude's monthly review finding F1. Written after returns-study step 4 (C1's 2008-inclusive figures were known), before any 2008-inclusive number for the 8-sleeve baseline was computed.
hypothesis: At a matched -15% worst drawdown over 2008-01..2026-06, the C1 core earns at least as much as the honest 8-sleeve baseline (within 0.5%/yr). If it doesn't, the owner's decision to retire momentum, sector rotation and trend at the switch should be reopened.
benchmark: BASELINE = honest 8-sleeve fund with the original weights HARD-CODED (not read from the allocation table): long_term_etf 25% (ma_bond_rotation_cs_b126 on QQQ IEF KMLM); momentum 15% (dual_momentum_long_only on SPY QQQ IWM EFA EEM GLD IEF TLT); sector_rotation 10% (relative_strength_b05 on the 11 SPDR sectors); trend_following 7.5% (ma_trend_long_only on SPY); volatility 5% (vix_band on SVXY with ^VIX); mean_reversion 15% + pullback 10% + breakouts 7.5% + cash reserve 5% in T-bills.

candidates.C1: 50% 60/40 SPY/IEF + 25% long_term_etf (same model as the baseline) + 25% T-bills
candidates.C3: POST-HOC: the baseline with sector_rotation, momentum and trend held equal-weight in their own instruments instead of timed

fairness: On both sides the idle share of every timed sleeve earns T-bills (SVXY didn't exist until late 2011, so its sleeve is T-bills before that). KMLM doesn't exist before 2021, so long_term_etf rotates QQQ/IEF only until then in BOTH the baseline and C1.
data: Total returns (adj_close), 10 bps per side, fills at the signal close, long-only; T-bills = ^IRX/252 lagged a day; daily fixed weights

pass_rule.method: scale each portfolio with T-bills (k<1) or margin (k>1, borrowing at T-bill + spread) so its worst 2008-01..2026-06 drawdown equals the budget, as in returns-study step 4
pass_rule.decision: C1 is REAFFIRMED if CAGR(C1 at -15%) >= CAGR(baseline at -15%) - 0.5%/yr at the primary spread; otherwise REOPEN.

also_reported: unscaled CAGR/Sharpe/max DD 2008-2026 and by period (2008-10, 2011-15, 2016-20, 2021-26/06); exposure k each portfolio needs; each timed sleeve vs holding its own instruments in 2008-2010

consequences.reaffirmed: C1 goes to the ~10/11 review unchanged.
consequences.reopen: Present the result to the owner: keeping some or all timing sleeves inside the core becomes the question. C1 stays unmerged either way; nothing live changes from this test.
